title: A harness that drops earlier reasoning: growth is F plus visible output
brief: Today is {{TODAY}}. Harness: a terminal agent harness calling the Anthropic API. The harness reports this session's model as claude-opus-5-5 at effort high.
Its session header shows 600,000 tokens in use of a 1,000,000-token window; its documentation says it compacts at 97 percent of the window. This session has not been compacted.

This harness drops earlier reasoning from the context at each new turn. Over the last 10 turns the context grew by 3,800 tokens per turn (measured from the session header), while fresh input averaged 3,000 tokens per turn and output, reasoning included, 3,000 tokens per turn, of which 800 were visible (measured from the harness's usage log). The next stage is expected to behave the same way.
A fresh session in this harness and project starts at 86,450 tokens (measured from the session header before any message).
Next stage: scoped work inside one module (a new subcommand and its tests). The module does not touch authentication, payments, storage formats or a public interface. Plan estimate: 90 turns.
A fresh session would read 20,000 tokens: the handoff and the module.
A handoff for this stage would be about 80 lines.
Everything this session knows that the next stage needs is already written in files on disk.
No cache-miss measurement exists, and no review pauses are expected during the stage.
The stage writes files and commits locally; nothing leaves the machine.

alternatives.why: the reading G = F + O, with F 3,000 as measured: step 1.3's default when growth is not measured

notes: The calculator has no growth input: G is F + O. Growth of F plus visible output (3,000 + 800 = 3,800) is entered as an effective F of 800 (3,800 less O), which keeps every output token billed at the output rate and writes to cache only what stays in context.

The alternative reading (F 3,000, G 6,000) crosses K and the main reading does not; the verdict is fresh by cost either way. A subject's block may state G 3,800 with F 3,000; the scorer recomputes with F = G - O (eval/rubric.md, measure 3).
